title: Batari Indra 01 (NSIC Rc 406H) Hybrid Rice: Yield, Maturity and Characteristics
metaTitle: Batari Indra 01 (NSIC Rc 406H) Rice: Yield and Maturity
metaDescription: Batari Indra 01 is NSIC Rc 406H, a hybrid rice for irrigated lowland: about 112 days and 5.9 tonnes per hectare on average. See its ratings.
excerpt: NSIC Rc 406H is a hybrid rice variety for irrigated lowland, sold as Batari Indra 01 or Batari Indra and known locally as Mestiso 67. The NSIC approved it in 2015. Bayer bred it, and Aljay sells it under its own brand, Batari Indra 01. It matures in about 112 days and averages 5.9 tonnes per hectare, with a top yield of 10.9 tonnes in trials.

blocks.text: How much does NSIC Rc 406H yield?

On average it gives 5.9 tonnes per hectare. That is about 118 cavans of 50 kilograms of palay. It sits below the average of the 180 irrigated lowland hybrids on the list, which is 6.9 tonnes. But the top yield, 10.9 tonnes, came from a trial with good water, seed and care. So plan your costs on the average, then work toward the top with the habits in our guide to [raising rice yield per hectare](/blog/increase-rice-yield-per-hectare).
How many days does it take to mature?

It takes about 112 days from sowing to harvest. Varieties of 100 to 120 days count as short duration and 120 to 140 days as medium, so this one counts as short duration. Then harvest when 85 to 90 percent of the grains turn golden yellow. Because the day count drives every task, anee.io counts it for you from each lot's own planting day, with the [growth stages and weather](/features/growth-stages-and-weather) beside it.

blocks.text: So scout early for [tungro](/diseases/rice-tungro), [sheath blight](/diseases/sheath-blight). When you see the first signs, check the guide before you spray, because the right timing saves more than an extra dose. If you are not sure what you see, our [pest and disease finders](/features/pest-and-disease-finders) help you name it from the damage.

Amylose decides how rice cooks. With intermediate amylose, expect rice that is soft but not sticky. In fact, Filipino taste has moved from high to intermediate and low amylose rice, because people want it softer. Head rice is the share of whole grains after milling. So a higher number means fewer broken grains and a better price at the mill.

items: Sold by Aljay, a farm supply company in Santiago, Isabela, under its Batari brand.
A sturdy plant that stays standing and does not lodge.

blocks.text: These are the seller's own figures, from its own trials. So plant a small area first, and compare it with your usual variety on the same ground.

It suits irrigated lowland, where you control the water. Level the field well so the water stands evenly, and plant at the same time as your neighbors, so pests cannot move from field to field. Our guide to [rice land preparation](/land-preparation/rice-land-preparation) shows each step. It is recommended for the dry season and the wet season. You can plant it dry direct seeded, transplanted or wet direct seeded. For the right month in your province, see [the best time to plant rice](/blog/best-time-to-plant-rice-philippines).

items.q: Is Batari Indra 01 the same as NSIC Rc 406H?
items.a: Yes. Batari Indra 01 is the name it is sold under, and NSIC Rc 406H is its registration with the National Seed Industry Council, where its local name is Mestiso 67. The numbers on this page are for NSIC Rc 406H.

items.q: What is the local name of NSIC Rc 406H?
items.a: It is known as Mestiso 67. Seed sellers and agriculturists use both names, so ask for either one.

items.q: How many days does NSIC Rc 406H take to harvest?
items.a: About 112 days after sowing. Then harvest when 85 to 90 percent of the grains are golden yellow.

items.q: What is the average yield of NSIC Rc 406H?
items.a: It averages 5.9 tonnes per hectare, about 118 cavans of 50 kilograms. The best trial reached 10.9 tonnes. Your own yield depends on water, seed, fertilizer and timing.

items.q: In which season should I plant it?
items.a: It is recommended for the dry season and the wet season. Then pick the month with our planting calendar guide and the forecast for your town.
Yes. So buy new seed each season, because seed saved from a hybrid crop does not grow true and yields less.
